rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the deniers reject proofs from creation and provision, the Prophet's task is to perfect knowledge of God and service to Him; Razi links this to 20:130.
rows.anchor: أن تكمل في نفسك وهو علمك بربك وعملك لربك

rows.speaker: المشهور
rows.claim: The common parsing treats “name” as extra; mentioning God's name still intensifies reverence, since the truly exalted are named only with descriptions of greatness.
rows.anchor: هو المشهور وهو أن الاسم مقحم ، وعلى هذا الجواب فنقول : فيه فائدة زيادة التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb can take its object with or without a preposition when the relation is intermediate in clarity; because tasbih really targets the Lord through the name, the hidden relation permits bāʾ.
rows.anchor: إذا كان بينهما جاز الوجهان فنقول : سبحته وسبحت به وشكرته وشكرت له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, bāʾ is meaningful: idolaters concede God created everything but call idols gods by name, so they must not assign the divine name to anything besides Him; the admonition addresses any hearer.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر الأمور وقال : نحن أم أنتم ، فاعترف الكل بأن الأمور من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command is to glorify God by naming Him aloud among one's people, describing Him and continuing to preach even if they refuse; a purely inward tasbih would not convey this.
rows.anchor: فسبح ربك بذكر اسمه بين قومك واشتغل بالتبليغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi also allows taking the phrase as beginning with the name of the Lord, making bāʾ nonredundant.
rows.anchor: فسبح مبتدئا باسم ربك العظيم فلا تكون الباء زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih is inward belief that God is one, without partner, and able rather than incapable of resurrection, or verbal praise such as “Subhan Allah,” or equivalent words.
rows.anchor: فبأن يعتقد فيه أنه واحد منزه عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Real divine unity excludes body, accident, location, and being in, on, or from anything; affirming God's power entails knowledge, will, life, and other attributes, discussed further in al-Ikhlas.
rows.anchor: لزم أن لا يكون جسما لأن الجسم فيه أشياء كثيرة وهو واحد حقيقي لا كثرة لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi distinguishes the epithets: perceptible greatness suggests nearness to all, while absolute elevation suggests remoteness from everything; God transcends perception, and positive attributes exceed what knowledge reaches.
rows.anchor: أما الفرق بين العظيم والأعلى فهو أن العظيم يدل على القرب ، والأعلى يدل على البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Higher” directly conveys transcendence, while “greater” combines an affirmative notion with a negative one; Razi therefore judges “al-Aʿlā” the more apt usage.
rows.anchor: فالأعلى مستعمل على حقيقته لفظا ومعنى ، والأعظم مستعمل على حقيقته لفظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowlā here means “why not?” and is one of four exhortative particles: lawmā, halā, and alā are the others; Razi traces them to “why not?”
rows.anchor: كلمات التحضيض وهي أربع كلمات : لولا ، ولوما ، وهلا ، وألا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogation can deny an act or its cause. A question with hal denies the act itself, while a question with lim denies its cause, implying the act would otherwise have reason to occur.
rows.anchor: فالاستفهام ( بهل ) لإنكار الفعل ، والاستفهام ( بلم ) لإنكار سببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negative or prohibitive speech can allude to denial instead of directly calling the addressee a liar, avoiding the need to spell out the denial.
rows.anchor: فعرض بالنفي لئلا يحتاج إلى بيان النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi cites 56:81, 37:125, and 37:86 as examples of interrogative forms used for denial.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى ههنا : { أفبهاذا الحديث أنتم مدهنون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both hal and law generally imply two clauses, though one may be elided; law implies an unstated proof for the denied consequence, as also in 56:76.
rows.anchor: إن كل واحد منهما يقع في صدر الكلام ، ويستدعي كلاما مركبا من كلامين في الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negation through law or hal is stronger than through lā or lim; exhortative lawlā, lawmā, halā, and alā express “why do you not?” when action is needed.
rows.anchor: وإذا ثبت أن النفي بلو ، والنفي بهل ، أبلغ من النفي بلا ، والنفي بقوله : لم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added explicitness of alā increases both the wording and the force beyond its underlying “why not?” sense.
rows.anchor: فقد وجد في ألا زيادة نص ، لأن نقل اللفظ لا يخلو من نص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death, when reality is manifest, why do deniers not reject the messengers if their own claims are true? Razi says everyone believes then, but late faith is not accepted.
rows.anchor: { فلولا إذا بلغت الحلقوم } أي لم لا يقولون عند الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the objection that people may keep denying until death, Razi says death itself is undeniable and leaves no speech or opportunity to acquire faith; this warns them to seek truth beforehand.
rows.anchor: فإنهم وإن كفروا بالحشر وهو الحياة بعد الموت لكنهم لم ينكروا الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage also consoles the messengers: deniers will recant, and that recantation benefits them only if made before the death throes.
rows.anchor: فبشروا بأن المكذبين سيرجعون عما يقولون ، ثم هو إن كان قبل النزع فذلك مقبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “it reaches” can refer to the soul, life, or spirit.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { بلغت } للنفس أو للحياة أو الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You are then looking” confirms that events become visible and witnessed at that moment; the wording and meaning match the argument.
rows.anchor: تأكيد لبيان الحق أي في ذلك الوقت تصير الأمور مرئية مشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage connects with 56:46–47, where they persisted in grave sin and questioned resurrection after death, explicitly showing their denial.
rows.anchor: إنهم { وكانوا يصرون على الحنث العظيم * وكانوا يقولون * أءذا متنا } ( الواقعة : 46 ، 47 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reads the preceding references to rain and provision against polytheists' attribution of rain and other natural processes to celestial intermediaries or delegated causes.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : { أنزلتموه من المزن أم نحن المنزلون لو } ( الواقعة : 69 ) بالواسطة وبالتفويض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking rizq to mean livelihood is more direct than supplying the meaning “gratitude” to the phrase about their provision.
rows.anchor: وأما جعل الرزق بمعنى المعاش فأقرب ، يقال : فلان رزقه في لسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The connection with 29:63 is that when asked who sends rain and revives the earth, they answer “God,” despite their denial of the messengers.
rows.anchor: لقوله تعالى : { ولئن سألتهم من نزل من السماء ماء فأحيا به الارض من بعد موتها ليقولن الله }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Razi cites a saying attributed to the Prophet that astrologers lie, as part of the argument about their denial and claims.
rows.anchor: كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( كذب المنجمون ورب الكعبة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On a reading that lightens takdhib, the passage contrasts their denial of the messengers with their affirmation that God sends rain.
rows.anchor: وهذا على قراءة من يقرأ { تكذبون } بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about mudāhana remains in its original sense and agrees with 68:9: they wanted the Prophet to compromise so they would compromise; it means hypocrisy, not open denial.
rows.anchor: فإن المراد هناك ليس تكذب فيكذبون ، لأنهم أرادوا النفاق لا التكذيب الظاهر

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes treat the second lawlā as a repetition of the first, with one answer.
rows.anchor: أكثر المفسرين على أن ( لولا ) في المرة الثانية مكررة وهي بعينها هي التي قال تعالى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī gives the answer as asking why they do not return the soul when it reaches the throat if they are not subject to judgment.
rows.anchor: وتقديره على ما قاله الزمخشري : فلولا ترجعونها إذا بلغت الحلقوم ، أي إن كنتم غير مدينين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some compare the construction to 2:38, where one response serves two conditional clauses.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : هو كقوله تعالى : { فإما يأتينكم منى هدى فمن تبع هداي فلا خوف عليهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects those readings: the first lawlā's answer is implied by the prior challenge about denial during life and at death, while the second lawlā is answered by “you would return it.”
rows.anchor: والظاهر خلاف ما قالوا ، وهو أن يقال : جواب لولا في قوله : { فلولا إذا بلغت الحلقوم }

rows.speaker: منهم من قال
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes madīnīn to mean owned or enslaved.
rows.anchor: في { مدينين } أقوال منهم من قال : المراد مملوكين

rows.speaker: منهم من قال
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes madīnīn to mean recompensed.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال : مجزيين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains madīnīn as governed by a ruler, from dānah al-sulṭān, “he governed him.”
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : من دانه السلطان إذا ساسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi proposes madīnīn might mean settled residents, from madana, “to dwell.”
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقال : المراد غير مقيمين من مدن إذا أقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the resident reading, madīnīn follows the faʿīl pattern; madīna and madāʾin illustrate the formation, while the mafʿila reading would retain a yāʾ in the plural, as in maʿāyish.
rows.anchor: هو حينئذ فعيل ، ومنه المدينة ، وجمعها مدائن ، من غير إظهار الياء ، ولو كانت مفعلة لكان جمعها مداين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If madīnīn means those recompensed, the challenge targets people who deny any punishment or its permanence: if no lasting punishment awaits, why not return themselves to worldly life?
rows.anchor: كان قوم ينكرون العذاب الدائم ، وقوم ينكرون العذاب ومن اعترف به كان ينكر دوامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it means recompensed, a world not devoted to recompense should leave them free to go wherever they wish, so their inability to return contradicts their denial of judgment.
rows.anchor: فإن التعويق للجزاء لا غير ، ولولا الجزاء لكنتم مختارين كما كنت في دنياكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it means owned or under another's rule, they should be able to return to the world they desire unless someone has power over them.
rows.anchor: إذا كنتم لستم تحت قدرة أحد ، فلم لا ترجعون أنفسكم إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretations converge against naturalist philosophers who assign rain, plants, and animals to nature and celestial causes while denying God's choice; if their view holds, their learned naturalist should restore the soul.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يقولون بالطبائع ، وأن الأمطار من السحب ، وهي متولدة بأسباب فلكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their own account allows survival through food and disease treatment, yet they cannot return the soul from the throat; this exposes the weakness of their claim.
rows.anchor: فإن عندهم البقاء بالغداء وزوال الأمراض بالدواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing death and the necessity of resurrection, the next passage describes the afterlife to motivate righteous action and deter rebellion and falsehood.
rows.anchor: ثم لما بين أن الموت كائن والحشر بعده لازم ، بين ما يكون بعد الحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledge terms themselves constitute the test of the women, so an additional command to test them is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: أن الامتحان حاصل بقوله تعالى : { على أن لا يشركن } إلى آخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike emigrants arriving from enemy territory without knowledge of Islamic law, women already in the Muslim polity know the law and need no separate test.
rows.anchor: أن المهاجرات يأتين من دار الحرب فلا اطلاع لهن على الشرائع

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: One explanation of “between their hands and feet” is that a woman takes an abandoned baby by hand and walks to fetch it, then falsely attributes it to her husband.
rows.anchor: من قال المرأة إذا التقطت ولدا ، فإنما التقطت بيدها ، ومشت إلى أخذه برجلها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they falsely claim a child as their own when it was born through adultery.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يفترينه على أنفسهن ، حيث يقلن : هذا ولدنا وليس كذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation is that the newborn falls between the mother's hands and feet.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الولد إذا وضعته أمه سقط بين يديها ورجليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listed prohibitions are ordered from the gravest to lesser offenses.
rows.anchor: قدم الأقبح على ما هو الأدنى منه في القبح ، ثم كذلك إلى آخره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explanation for the order is that the most conspicuous items come first.
rows.anchor: وقيل : قدم من الأشياء المذكورة ما هو الأظهر فيما بينهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the warning as referring to Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa and says not to ally with Jews and polytheists.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد حاطب ابن أبي بلتعة يقول : لا تتولوا اليهود والمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some poor Muslims disclosed Muslim affairs to the Jews because they needed their support, prompting the prohibition on alliance.
rows.anchor: لأن جمعا من فقراء المسلمين كانوا يخبرون اليهود أخبار المسلمين لحاجتهم إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews had rejected Muhammad despite knowing he was God's Messenger, thereby ruining their afterlife and despairing of it.
rows.anchor: يعني أن اليهود كذبت محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وهم يعرفون أنه رسول الله

rows.speaker: الكلبي وجماعة
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī and a group explain the comparison as dead unbelievers having given up hope of Paradise and any good in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو قول الكلبي وجماعة ، يعني الكفار الذين ماتوا يئسوا من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction to those who die in unbelief makes their lack of any afterlife share certain.
rows.anchor: لأنهم إذا ماتوا على كفرهم كان العلم بخذلانهم وعدم حظهم في الآخرة قطعيا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets the verse as the living unbelievers despairing of those already dead.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : يعني الأحياء من الكفار يئسوا من الأموات

rows.speaker: أبو إسحق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the Jews who opposed the Prophet despair of the afterlife as resurrection-denying unbelievers despair of their dead.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحق : يئس اليهود الذين عاندوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses ṭibāqan first as heavens stacked atop one another, by analogy with placing one layer upon another.
rows.anchor: ذكر صاحب ( الكشاف ) في { طباقا } ثلاثة أوجه أولها : طباقا أي مطابقة بعضها فوق بعض من طابق النعل إذا خصفها طبقا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: A second parse makes ṭibāqan describe heavens that possess layers.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أن يكون التقدير ذات طباق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: A third parse treats the phrase as an implicit passive construction, “layered in layers.”
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أن يكون التقدير طوبقت طباقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens demonstrate power because they hang in the air without pillars or chains.
rows.anchor: من حيث إنها بقيت في جو الهواء معلقة بلا عماد ولا سلسلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each heaven has a particular size, though a greater or smaller size was possible.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : من حيث إن كل واحد منها اختص بمقدار معين مع جواز ما هو أزيد منه وأنقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each heaven has a measured movement, speed, and direction.
rows.anchor: أنه اختص كل واحد منها بحركة خاصة مقدرة بقدر معين من السرعة والبطء إلى جهة معينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens are originated beings; together these features show dependence on an agent with complete power.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : كونها في ذواتها محدثة وكل ذلك يدل على استنادها إلى قادر تام القدرة

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the word with one of the two reported forms; the other readers use the alternate form.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي { من تفاوت } والباقون { من تفاوت }

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ considers the two readings equivalent, like taẓhar/taẓāhar and taʿahhad/taʿāhad.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : وهما بمنزلة واحدة مثل تظهر وتظاهر ، وتعهد وتعاهد

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash prefers tafāwut because Arabic speakers say “the matter differs” and rarely use the alternate form.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش : { تفاوت } أجود لأنهم يقولون : تفاوت الأمر ولا يكادون يقولون : تفوت

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda chooses tafāwut and supports the forms with reported usage and a report of a man who got ahead of his father in wealth.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو عبيدة : { تفاوت } ، وقال : يقال تفوت الشيء إذا فات ، واحتج بما روي في الحديث أن رجلا تفوت على أبيه في ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafāwut means lack of proportion: one part misses or fails to fit another; its opposite is proportion and harmony.
rows.anchor: حقيقة التفاوت عدم التناسب كأن بعض الشيء يفوت بعضه ولا يلائمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi illustrates the opposition with the expression “a disparate relation” versus “proportionate,” then explains that the next phrase may equate tafāwut with fuṭūr.
rows.anchor: ومنه قولهم : ( تعلق متعلق متفاوت ونقيضه متناسب )

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains it as defective variation, so a viewer might say the creation would be better if it were otherwise.
rows.anchor: فقال السدي : من تفاوت أي من اختلاف عيب ، يقول الناظر : لو كان كذا كان أحسن

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other exegetes take tafāwut as cracks or openings, supported by the following word fuṭūr and by 50:6.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : التفاوت الفطور بدليل قوله بعد ذلك : { فارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور }

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl suggests the phrase may mean there is no discrepancy in how creation signifies its maker's wisdom and purposive design.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى : ما ترى في خلق الرحمن من تفاوت في الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in “you see” and the command to look again may target the Messenger or any addressee.
rows.anchor: الخطاب في قوله : { ما ترى } إما للرسول أو لكل مخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭibāqan is one adjective for the heavens, and the no-discrepancy clause is a second; Razi supplies the implicit “in them.”
rows.anchor: وقوله بعد ذلك : { ما ترى فى خلق الرحمان من تفاوت } صفة أخرى للسموات والتقدير خلق سبع سموات طباقا ما ترى فيهن من تفاوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replacing the pronoun with “the creation of the Merciful” magnifies the heavens and explains their harmony through God's power.
rows.anchor: وضع مكان الضمير قوله : { خلق الرحمان } تعظيما لخلقهن وتنبيها على سبب سلامتهن من التفاوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inference to divine knowledge is that the seven heavens are created bodies made with exactness, and every maker whose work is exact must know.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن وجه الاستدلال بهذا على كمال علم الله تعالى هو أن الحس دل أن هذه السموات السبع ، أجسام مخلوقة على وجه الإحكام والإتقان

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Kaʿbī argues that the verse excludes God from creating sins: lack of discrepancy means lack of defects in wisdom, while human acts include ignorance, lies, and folly.
rows.anchor: احتج الكعبي بهذه الآية على أن المعاصي ليست من خلق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi replies that creation has no discrepancy relative to God, since all things occur through His power, will, and motive, and nothing is intrinsically ugly for Him; Kaʿbī has not shown his reading superior.
rows.anchor: بل نحن نحمله على أنه لا تفوت فيه بالنسبة إليه ، من حيث إن الكل يصح منه بحسب القدرة والإرادة والداعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to inspect again guards against error from a single glance and makes the absence of any flaw certain.
rows.anchor: ولا تعتمد عليه بسبب أنه قد يقع الغلط في النظرة الواحدة ، ولكن ارجع البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fuṭūr is the plural of faṭr, meaning a split; the verb describes splitting, including a camel tooth breaking through flesh.
rows.anchor: والفطور جمع فطر ، وهو الشق يقال : فطره فانفطر ومنه فطر ناب البعير

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes gloss fuṭūr as gaps, fissures, splits, openings, and holes.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : { هل ترى من فطور } أي من فروج وصدوع وشقوق ، وفتوق
